place_fields.summary: Haft Gumbad is a group of seven Bahmani-era royal tombs in Kalaburagi, representing early Indo-Islamic funerary architecture.

planning_attributes.description: A Bahmani royal tomb complex built in the 14th and 15th centuries, with seven tombs including the tomb of Firuz Shah Bahmani.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The complex was built during the Bahmani Sultanate period while Gulbarga was its capital. The tomb of Firuz Shah Bahmani is the largest of the group.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Located in Kalaburagi near the Gulbarga Fort area and reachable by local road transport.
planning_attributes.notes: The tomb complex is a monument of national importance maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

place_fields.summary: Kumaraswamy Temple at Krauncha Giri is an ancient Hindu temple complex near Sandur, set in a forested hill landscape.

planning_attributes.description: The Kumaraswami Temple dates to the 8th-10th century and is one of two ancient protected Hindu temples in the Krauncha Giri compound.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple is traditionally regarded as an early South Indian abode of Murugan or Karthikeya and is paired with the nearby Parvati Temple.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Krauncha Giri is about 10 km from Sandur. Sandur is connected by road; Toranagal is the nearest railway station at about 30 km.
planning_attributes.notes: The Kumaraswami and Parvati temples at Krauncha Giri are protected monuments.

place_fields.summary: Gulbarga Fort is a large medieval fortress in Kalaburagi associated with the Bahmani Sultanate and notable for its double fortification, moat, bastions and historic mosque.

planning_attributes.description: The fort was originally built by Raja Gulchand and later substantially fortified by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. It contains 15 bastions, 26 guns and the Jama Masjid.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Kalaburagi became the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, and the fort developed into a major political and military centre during the Bahmani period.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The fort is in central Kalaburagi and is reachable by road; Kalaburagi has rail, bus and airport connections.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The fort has uneven terrain and steps, so sturdy footwear and care while walking are advisable.
planning_attributes.notes: The fort covers about 20 acres, has a double fortification and a moat, and includes the Jama Masjid complex.
